page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server platform built for massive computing and memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The system is driven by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 144 physical cores and 288 dedicated execution threads operating at up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration capabilities including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions. Memory provision is dense, delivering 2232 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, which yields 7.75 GB per core. The server operates directly on bare metal without hypervisor virtualization layers, and contains no integrated local storage disks or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across parallelized execution streams. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and software compilation under Clang, backed by substantial memory bandwidth that reaches 1090.07 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 412.54 GB/sec on writes. Synthetic database evaluation and transactional memory testing show top-decile ratings, with Redis SET performance exceeding 423 million operations per second and static web throughput reaching 174.2 GB/sec. Large language model inference benchmarks demonstrate strong prompt processing throughput across 7B and 70B parameter models, although sequential token generation on smaller models is constrained by the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators.

The hardware configuration provides high physical resource density and memory allocation per core, making it cost-efficient for consolidating large memory footprints into a single host footprint without hypervisor latency. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of integrated local storage, requiring workloads to rely on remote block storage or external network filesystems. This server type is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases like Redis and SAP HANA, parallel CI/CD build environments, large enterprise ETL batch processing, and memory-bound scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server engineered for enterprise-scale compute and memory-intensive applications. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores using Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors clocked at 4.2 GHz, backed by a 504 MB L3 cache and hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server is configured with 2232 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 6 GHz, offering approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU and exceeding 1 TB/s in uncached read bandwidth. It features no integrated local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on remote network volumes for persistent storage. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, and in-memory key-value operations with over 400 million Redis operations per second. This hardware profile provides resource density for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale data processing, intensive scientific simulations, and continuous integration compilation pipelines.
